chunks: And it was narrated from Ayyūb, the brother of Udaym, who said:
Abū ʿAbdِ Allāh عليه السلام was asked, “From where are the children stripped (for ihram)?” So he said, “My father عليه السلام used to strip them at Fakh.”

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Imam Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام, the one being asked
key_terms.أَبِي: my father, referring to the preceding Imam عليه السلام
key_terms.أَيُّوبَ: Ayyūb, the narrator transmitting this report
key_terms.فَخٍّ: Fakh, a known location mentioned as the place of stripping for children
key_terms.يُجَرَّدُ: to be stripped of ordinary clothes for entering the state associated with ihram

ai.seo_question: From where should children be stripped for ihram during hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a fiqh ruling related to the hajj of children, specifically the place from which they are prepared for ihram. Imam Abū ʿAbdِ Allāh عليه السلام answers by citing the practice of his father عليه السلام, indicating Fakh as the point where children were stripped for the rite.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2894 - It was narrated from Ayyub, the brother of Udaym, who said:

Abu Abdullah (as) was asked: "From where are the children stripped (for Ihram)?"
Imam (as) said: "My father (as) used to strip them at Fakh."
